race_context: The district: Bloomfield School District in Greene County serves the town of Bloomfield and Highland, Richland and Taylor townships {wiki_bsd}. Its schools are Bloomfield Elementary School and Bloomfield Middle and High School {bsd_board}. Public School Review lists about 852 students in three schools; the year behind that figure is unclear {psr_bsd}. Dr. Scott Van Der Aa has been superintendent since the board hired him in March 2023 on a 5-1 vote {gcdw_bsup23}{gcdw_bsep26}.

Board: the board has seven members {gcdw_seats}. The district's board page lists three District 1 (Richland) members: Darren Burch (president), Chad J. Strange (vice president) and Terri Neighbors. It also lists Kayla Hendrix for District 2 (Highland), Lana Pinnick (secretary) for District 3 (Taylor), and Casey Michael and Steve Dowden at large {bsd_board}. In January 2025 the board appointed Michael to an at-large seat that no candidate had filed for in the 2024 election {gcdw_bsel}{gcdw_res24}.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: the seats elected in 2022 come up again in 2026. In 2022, Neighbors and Strange won the two District 1 seats, Hendrix won District 2 unopposed, and Pinnick won District 3 over Keith Bennett, 987 to 887 votes {gcdw_b22win}. Of those four members, only Strange (District 1) and Pinnick (District 3) are on the 2026 ballot {in_list}{gcdw_seats}. Neighbors and Hendrix are not running, so at least one District 1 seat and the District 2 seat will go to a newcomer.

Seat count: the state list shows District 1 as “vote for 1,” but District 1 filled two seats in 2022 {gcdw_b22win} and has three members in all {bsd_board}. That points to two District 1 seats on the 2026 ballot. No fetched 2026 source states the number of District 1 seats. The Daily World's 2026 ballot list gives District 1 six candidates without saying how many will win {gcdw_seats}.

Party labels: on the state list, Aaron Wilson, Chad J Strange, Darla Lynn Chesnut, Jessica Blazier, Leland E Hutchens and Keith Bennett are Republican. Blake D. Burch, Kaitilyn Elizabeth Harvey and Lana J. Pinnick are Nonpartisan {in_list}.

Facilities and bonds: in August and September 2026 the board took steps toward its next bond project. It approved the form of lease and reapproved the building corporation, appointed a technical review committee, hired The Rawlins Group LLC as design criteria developer, and passed resolutions on project need, construction bids, appropriations and the issuing of bonds {gcdw_baug26}{gcdw_bsep26}. Earlier, in 2025, science, chemistry and art classrooms at the middle/high school were renovated {gcdw_boct25}.

Budget: the board approved the 2026 budget, capital projects plan and bus replacement plan in September 2025, and the 2027 versions on Sept. 24, 2026 {gcdw_boct25}{gcdw_bsep26}. No fetched source covered how the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1) affects Bloomfield, and none mentioned an operating or safety referendum.

Programs: the district has been building a child care center (Chirps Childcare), which was nearing completion in September 2026. It is also creating a cybersecurity career pathway with Project Lead The Way and College Board, and has formed a Next Generation School Improvement Plan steering committee {gcdw_boct25}{gcdw_bsep26}. The board accepted Secured School Safety grants of $87,875 in 2025 and $85,226 in 2026 {gcdw_boct25}{gcdw_bsep26}.

Forum: seven candidates appeared at a “Meet the Candidates” event at the Shawnee Theatre in Bloomfield on Thursday, Sept. 17, 2026, moderated by Brent Seymour; Leland Hutchens was not present {gcdw_forum}. The Daily World reported that candidates “by and large” agreed on working with staff and administration, and differed mainly in personal experience, reasons for running and familiarity with school policy {gcdw_forum}.

Differences in candidate statements: Strange and Blazier spoke well of the district's current spending, and Pinnick cited her experience keeping the district financially sound {gcdw_bios}. Chesnut said she is concerned about recent turnover of teachers and administrators and about outdated textbooks {gcdw_chesnut}. Bennett said some changes in the district left “more questions than answers” {gcdw_bw}.

candidates.summary: Foster-care child advocate and former instructional assistant at Bloomfield High School, running in District 1; listed as Nonpartisan {in_list}{gcdw_bios}.
background: Graduated from Bloomfield High School in 2020 and lives in Richland Township {gcdw_bios}.
Since January 2024 has worked for a local government program that advocates for children in foster care or involved in custody disputes {gcdw_bios}.

After a service year with AmeriCorps' FEMA Corps program, he returned to Bloomfield in fall 2023. He worked briefly as an instructional assistant in the high school library and remains sponsor of the high school Beta Club {gcdw_bios}.

Serves on the board of directors of Shawnee Summer Theatre and on the Greene County 4-H Council, leads a Bloomfield 4-H club, and teaches local Parents Forever and Strengthening Families classes {gcdw_bios}.
path_to_ballot: Listed on the state ballot list as Nonpartisan for District 1 {in_list}{gcdw_seats}.
Attended the Sept. 17, 2026 Meet the Candidates event {gcdw_forum}.
on_incumbent: No statement about the current board's decisions was found in fetched sources.
plans: Says he is running to serve the community and its young people {gcdw_bios}.
endorsements_finance: No endorsements or campaign finance reports were found in fetched sources.

candidates.summary: Incumbent and board vice president, seeking reelection to a District 1 (Richland) seat; safety and operations manager for Nutrien Ag Solutions; listed as Republican {in_list}{bsd_board}{gcdw_bios}.
background: Is the board's vice president, holding a District 1 Richland seat {bsd_board}. He was first elected in 2022 with 943 votes {gcdw_b22win}.
Works for Nutrien Ag Solutions as safety and operations manager of its Switz City and Odon locations, and is a graduate of Bloomfield High School and Vincennes University {gcdw_bios}.
Parent of two students in the district {gcdw_bios}.
path_to_ballot: Listed on the state ballot list as Republican for District 1 {in_list}{gcdw_seats}.
Attended the Sept. 17, 2026 Meet the Candidates event {gcdw_forum}.

items: Said schools are being asked to do more with less funding, and that the board has been innovative with its money, thanks partly to a fiscally responsible superintendent and treasurer {gcdw_bios}.
In 2022 he said his main goal was “to bring the taxpayers voices back to the voting floor, and ensure that the will of the voters is being done” {gcdw_b22forum}.
At a 2022 forum he said teachers in the district need to be taken care of {gcdw_b22forum}.
Says he has made it a priority to listen to anyone who contacts him, calling that his “elected duty” {gcdw_bios}.

on_incumbent: Is a current board member. Says he is proud of what the board has done to make sure every student gets the best education the district can provide {gcdw_bios}.
In January 2025 he nominated Brian Cahill, who was not selected, for the vacant at-large seat; the board appointed Casey Michael on a 4-2 vote, with Strange voting for Cahill {gcdw_bsel}.
plans: Says that if reelected he will keep representing stakeholders, faculty, staff and students {gcdw_bios}.
endorsements_finance: No endorsements or campaign finance reports were found in fetched sources.
gaps: His voting record on major items, such as the 2023 superintendent hire and the 2026 bond resolutions, was not broken out by member in fetched sources.
No candidate website or questionnaire was found.

candidates.summary: Works in accounting at Metal Technologies Inc. and is a longtime community-event volunteer, running in District 1; listed as Republican {in_list}{gcdw_chesnut}.
background: Works in the accounting department at Metal Technologies Inc. in Bloomfield {gcdw_chesnut}.

Has been on the Bloomfield Apple Festival Committee for about 25 years, mostly as secretary or treasurer, and organizes the town's Easter egg hunt, Light up the Park and Lighted Parade {gcdw_chesnut}.
Has grandchildren at Bloomfield Elementary and Bloomfield High School {gcdw_chesnut}.
path_to_ballot: Listed on the state ballot list as Republican for District 1 {in_list}{gcdw_seats}.
Attended the Sept. 17, 2026 Meet the Candidates event {gcdw_forum}.

items: Says she is running because she is concerned about recent turnover of teachers and administrators: “An employee doesn't leave a job they love; they leave because they do not feel valued” {gcdw_chesnut}.
Says teachers should be allowed to teach without being micromanaged and should be treated as professionals, which she says would help retain current teachers {gcdw_chesnut}.
Says some teachers are using textbooks more than 10 years old, and that the curriculum should be kept up to date with updated resources {gcdw_chesnut}.

on_incumbent: Points to recent teacher and administrator turnover and outdated textbooks as concerns, without naming specific board decisions {gcdw_chesnut}.
plans: Says providing stability and updated resources would set students up to succeed {gcdw_chesnut}.

Parent of a fourth grader at Bloomfield Elementary {gcdw_bw}.

candidates.summary: Incumbent and board secretary, seeking a third term in the District 3 (Taylor) seat; works for the district as a bus driver and paraprofessional; listed as Nonpartisan {in_list}{bsd_board}{gcdw_bios}.

Has lived in Taylor Township her whole life; she has two grandchildren at Bloomfield Elementary {gcdw_bios}.

At a 2022 forum she said pushing for state funding to keep technology updated, and keeping trust and communication with administrators, were key to keeping qualified teachers {gcdw_b22forum}.
In 2022 she said she wanted enrollment to keep increasing {gcdw_b22forum}.
